subject: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / deployment / SLA clarification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finova.com>, Aditi Sharma <aditi@finova.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / deployment / SLA clarification

Thanks again for the time earlier, Sanjay — good conversation. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can align our proposal to Finova's decision criteria.

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Economic buyer: you (Sanjay) leading the evaluation, procurement loop via Aditi (procurement) + Michael (legal).
- Primary use: customer support assistant and KYC document summarization; expected average request size ~200-800 tokens.
- Security: SOC 2 + encryption-in-transit and at-rest required; likely a private/VPC deployment preference but open to Dedicated if it meets controls.

Clarifying questions (so our SOW and pricing match):
1) Latency targets — you mentioned target for user-facing flows of p95 < 300ms and p99 < 750ms for 512-token completions. Can you confirm these are strict targets or guidance? Any separate targets for longer async batch jobs?
2) Cost envelope — do you have a monthly inference spend target or a $/1k-token target we should aim for in the pricing model?
3) Deployment mode — preference for Private (VPC) due to data residency, or would you consider Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) if it reduces unit cost while meeting SOC2 and network controls?
4) SLA requirements — is 99.9% availability acceptable, and what are your response/priority targets for incident handling and security escalations?

Next steps: if you can confirm the latency and budget targets and introduce the procurement and security contacts (Aditi/Michael copied), we will:
- Share a focused latency/cost profile and deployment matrix (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Populate the security QA spreadsheet and return it within two business days.
- Propose a follow-up with your security/procurement leads to walk controls and SLA language.

Attachments: we'll attach a short latency/cost profile and a security QA template for completion.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if it helps.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditi Sharma <aditi@finova.com>, Michael Green <michael.green@finova.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finova decision criteria: latency / cost / deployment / SLA clarification

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers: 

1) Latency: the p95 < 300ms is a firm target for real-time support UI (we need snappy UX). p99 < 750ms is a target we expect to meet for >95% of traffic but can tolerate short spikes. For async/analytics batches (nightly), latency is not strict.
2) Cost: procurement will want an example monthly burn for a realistic pilot (100k active monthly users, ~300k requests). Ballpark target for pilot: keep inference spend under $25k/mo.
3) Deployment: initial preference is Private (VPC) because of data residency + some on-prem routing. If Dedicated can be demonstrated to meet SOC2 + network isolation and reduce cost materially, procurement will evaluate it.
4) SLA: 99.9% is standard; for security incidents we need a 1-hour initial response for sev1 and a named escalation contact.

Introduce: Aditi (procurement) and Michael (legal) are on copy — they'll coordinate contracts and budget signoff. Please include a security-runbook excerpt and explicit network connectivity options in your follow-up.

Sanjay
Head of Product
Finova

Looping in a couple quick clarifications from our side before we send the package to Finova: 

- Confirming what counts toward the SLA: is Finova expecting the SLA to apply to the Redwood control plane only, or to overall inference (incl. any customer-managed networking/VPC connectivity)? We should clarify scope in the SOW.
- For latency guarantees (p95/p99), we'll include profiling across model families and sequence lengths; want to confirm target token budgets — Sanjay mentioned ~200-800 tokens per call.
- For Private/VPC deployments: note that some features (e.g., streaming debug/traces) may be limited in fully air-gapped setups; we'll call these out.

Attachments: attaching the Security QA template we've used previously for enterprise deals and a short Latency/Cost profile that maps expected p95/p99 numbers across deployment modes.

Vivek
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Sanjay + team — great, that helps. Quick action plan from Redwood: 

1) Security & controls: Vivek and Rafael will complete the security QA and back it up with SOC2 evidence and our KMS integration notes. You'll get the completed spreadsheet by end of day tomorrow. (Attachment: Finova_Security_QA.xlsx)
2) Latency/Cost profile: attached a short PDF mapping p95/p99 across Hosted / Dedicated / Private with estimated monthly cost for a 100k-user pilot. We'll target figures that keep pilot inference spend < $25k/mo while meeting the p95 < 300ms target where possible. (Attachment: Redwood_Latency_Cost_Profiles.pdf)
3) SLA language: initial proposal will include 99.9% uptime, 1-hour sev1 response, and named escalation contacts. We'll flag control-plane vs customer-network scope for your legal to review.
4) Next call: propose a 30-minute session with your procurement + security leads tomorrow (Aug 12) at 10:00 AM PDT to walk the QA and SLA. If that works, we'll send a calendar invite and include a short runbook excerpt.

Links: HubSpot deal (for your ref) — https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/FIN-2026-042. For contracting we can start a DocuSign draft once procurement confirms budget.

If that schedule works, Aditi/Michael — please confirm and we will lock the invite.

Best,
Marissa
